study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the aim to integrate a normative model with non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) to quantify neuroanatomical heterogeneity in OCD, relate factor compositions to clinical variables, derive group-level differences from individualized patterns, and identify subtypes.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We propose a comprehensible framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) to quantitatively estimate the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD... Factor compositions of patients were significantly correlated with severity of symptom, age of onset, illness duration... the group-level morphological differences obtained with two-sample t test could be quantitatively derived from the identified disease factors... we uncovered two distinct subtypes with opposite morphological differences compared with HCs.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study builds a new normative model using healthy controls. It reports the reference cohort sample size (HCs n=130) and general exclusion criteria applied to all participants. However, explicit image quality standards and detailed reasons for post-acquisition exclusions are not described in the provided materials.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: T1-weighted magnetic resonance images of 98 first-episode untreated patients with OCD and matched healthy controls (HCs, n = 130) were acquired. ... all participants ... had to meet the following exclusion criteria: (i) taking drugs ...; (ii) substance abuse; (iii) a history of a brain tumor, trauma, surgery, or other organic body diseases; (iv) suffering from cardiovascular diseases, diabetes or hypertension; (v) contraindications for MRI scanning; and (vi) other structural brain abnormalities.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Then, we performed two-sample t test ... controlling age, sex, and TIV using SPM 12.
